conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: Hi, I'm Dr. Lee. I understand you're here with abdominal pain again?

conversation_lines.speaker: Patient
conversation_lines.text: Yes, same pain as last time, but worse. It's in the right lower side again.

conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: I see. And how’s your bowel movement? Any blood?

conversation_lines.speaker: Patient
conversation_lines.text: No blood, but I’ve had about 22 watery black stools in the last day. I don’t know why they’re black.

conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: That’s important. Black stools can mean digested blood, but it could also be from something you ate or medication. We’ll check that.

conversation_lines.speaker: Patient
conversation_lines.text: I haven’t changed my diet. I’ve been eating even with the pain.

conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: Good. We also saw you had a cough and sweats. Are those still going on?

conversation_lines.speaker: Patient
conversation_lines.text: Yeah, the sweats have been there for about a week. And I’ve got this cough with dark sputum, not bloody, but kind of blackish.

conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: Any fever or chills?

conversation_lines.speaker: Patient
conversation_lines.text: No, no fever. Just the sweats and the headache around my left eye.

conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: Okay. Given your history of Crohn’s disease, and the fact that you were just discharged five days ago, this sounds like a flare-up.

conversation_lines.speaker: Patient
conversation_lines.text: But I was feeling better after the last hospital stay. Why is it back so soon?

conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: Sometimes Crohn’s can relapse quickly, especially if the taper on steroids is too fast or if there’s ongoing inflammation.

conversation_lines.speaker: Patient
conversation_lines.text: I was on 55 mg prednisone when I left. Is that not enough?

conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: It might not be. We’ll restart IV steroids to get better control. You’ll also get IV fluids since you’ve had a lot of diarrhea.

conversation_lines.speaker: Patient
conversation_lines.text: Will I be able to eat?

conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: We’ll keep you NPO for now—nothing by mouth—to let your gut rest. Once things settle, we’ll start you on liquids and then soft food.

conversation_lines.speaker: Patient
conversation_lines.text: Okay. And my pain? It’s pretty bad.

conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: We’ve given you morphine in the ER, and we’ll continue pain meds through the IV. But we’ll avoid long-term opioids.

conversation_lines.speaker: Patient
conversation_lines.text: I don’t want to depend on them. But I need relief.

conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: We’ll manage it carefully. We also restarted your Imuran—azathioprine—to help control the immune response long-term.

conversation_lines.speaker: Patient
conversation_lines.text: I remember that from before. It didn’t work well last time because of kidney issues.

conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: Your kidney function is normal now, so it should be safe. We’ll monitor your labs closely.

conversation_lines.speaker: Patient
conversation_lines.text: What about the CT scan I had earlier?

conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: It showed mild inflammation around the sigmoid colon, but no blockage or abscess. It looks chronic, not new.

conversation_lines.speaker: Patient
conversation_lines.text: So it’s not something else? Like an infection?

conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: We tested your stool. No Salmonella, Shigella, C. diff, or other infections. So it’s likely your Crohn’s acting up.

conversation_lines.speaker: Patient
conversation_lines.text: What about the sweats and cough? Could that be related?

conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: Unlikely. Your lungs are clear on exam. The sweats were there last time too, and no infection was found. We’ll keep an eye on it.

conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: Good morning. You’re looking better. You’ve had less pain overnight and only four loose stools.

conversation_lines.speaker: Patient
conversation_lines.text: Yeah, the pain is more manageable. Can I try some food?

conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: Yes, we’ll start you on clear liquids. If that goes well, we’ll move to a soft diet tomorrow.

conversation_lines.speaker: Patient
conversation_lines.text: And the IV steroids? How long will I be on those?

conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: We’ll switch you to oral prednisone tomorrow. You’ll take 50 mg daily and taper slowly as directed by your GI doctor.

conversation_lines.speaker: Patient
conversation_lines.text: I hope this time the taper doesn’t cause a relapse.

conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: We’ll make it slower this time. And staying on Imuran should help prevent flares.

conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: You’re doing well. You’ve been on a regular diet since yesterday with no issues.

conversation_lines.speaker: Patient
conversation_lines.text: I feel much better. The sweats have stopped too.

conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: Great. Your labs are stable. WBC is still a bit high, but that’s expected with inflammation.

conversation_lines.speaker: Patient
conversation_lines.text: And my vitamin D? I remember they said it was low last time.

conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: Yes, you’re supposed to be on 800 IU daily. We’ve added a prescription for 400 IU twice a day to make it easier.

conversation_lines.speaker: Patient
conversation_lines.text: Is that enough? Should I get more sun?

conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: The supplement should help. But quitting smoking would do more for your overall health and Crohn’s control.

conversation_lines.speaker: Patient
conversation_lines.text: I know, I know. I’ve tried patches before.

conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: We can set you up with another patch and counseling. It really does make a difference.

conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: Today we’re planning for discharge tomorrow morning.

conversation_lines.speaker: Patient
conversation_lines.text: That’s good news. What meds will I be on?

conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: Prednisone 10 mg daily—take five tablets, then reduce by one tablet each week. Also, continue Imuran 50 mg daily, pantoprazole, and quetiapine.

conversation_lines.speaker: Patient
conversation_lines.text: No pain meds?

conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: No opioids. If you need relief, use acetaminophen. We want to avoid dependency.

conversation_lines.speaker: Patient
conversation_lines.text: And the vitamin D?

conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: Yes, two capsules a day—400 IU each. Take it with food for better absorption.

conversation_lines.speaker: Patient
conversation_lines.text: I need to get labs done before seeing my GI doctor?

conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: Yes, check CBC and liver tests one day before your appointment. Fax the results to her office.

conversation_lines.speaker: Patient
conversation_lines.text: What if my symptoms come back?

conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: Call your doctor or come back if you have worsening pain, vomiting, fever over 101, or dark or bloody stools.

conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: Good morning. You’re cleared to go home.

conversation_lines.speaker: Patient
conversation_lines.text: Thanks. I feel a lot better than when I came in.

conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: You’ve responded well. Keep up with your meds, the lab work, and follow-up. And please consider the smoking cessation program.

conversation_lines.speaker: Patient
conversation_lines.text: I will. Thank you for taking care of me again.

conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: Take care. We’re here if you need us.
